name: Axiom Systems Neural Disruptor ND-2 'Migraine'
description: A directed electromagnetic weapon specifically tuned to interfere with neural interface frequencies. The ND-2 projects a modulated electromagnetic field that induces cascading errors in neural implant firmware, causing effects ranging from sensory hallucination to complete motor shutdown depending on the target's implant architecture and shielding. Against unaugmented targets, the weapon has minimal effect — a mild headache at most. Against heavily augmented targets, it can be incapacitating or lethal if the neural interface manages autonomous functions like cardiac regulation.
specifications:
field type: Modulated neural-frequency electromagnetic pulse
effective range: 5-15 meters directional
target discrimination: Neural interface signatures only
power source: Dedicated capacitor pack, 15 pulses per charge
recharge: 4 seconds between pulses
weight: 2.1 kg
effect duration: 10-60 seconds depending on target shielding
story_hooks: Axiom officially denies the ND-2 exists, but units keep appearing in the hands of anti-augmentation extremist groups — someone inside Axiom is arming the movement.
A player character's neural interface begins experiencing intermittent glitches consistent with low-level ND-2 exposure — someone nearby is carrying one, but who?

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular directed-energy device resembling a hybrid between a surgical instrument and a compact railgun. The ND-2 has a pronounced forward-swept profile with a prominent emitter array at the muzzle, flanked by stabilizing fins. It reads as aggressive yet clinical — a tool of precise, surgical violence rather than blunt force.
physical_description.dimensions: 48 cm length, 12 cm width at widest point (grip), 8 cm height. Emitter array projects 6 cm forward of main body. Capacitor pack extends 14 cm along underside.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but manageable — 2.1 kg distributed toward the rear grip. Feels anchored and serious in hand, with subtle forward weight bias from the emitter assembly. Not unwieldy, but demands respect.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium-composite frame with integrated heat-sink ribbing. Polymer reinforced grip section. Emitter array is ceramic-shrouded conductive composite to contain field bleed.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal with high-contrast brushed titanium accents. Emitter shroud has faint iridescent oil-slick patina from electromagnetic field exposure. Light surface scoring from field calibration.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, brushed silver emitter shroud, deep blue capacitor pack casing. Faint amber glow from status LEDs on the grip module.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with integral finger grooves — engineered for precision aiming rather than rapid-fire. Slightly tacky to prevent slippage during neural targeting sequences.
distinctive_features: Forward-swept emitter array with hexagonal radiator fins
Two amber status LEDs (charge/ready indicator) on grip housing
Calibration alignment rails along the top — precision targeting mounts
Subtle vibration feedback port on rear grip for discharge confirmation
Capacitor pack casing with faint luminescent ink circuit tracery visible under certain light
Muzzle shroud with microscopic targeting reticle etched into ceramic
Heat vents along the sides resembling a heatsink — aesthetic and functional
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS logo (stylized Φ within a circuit loop) stamped in silver on left grip panel. Model designation 'ND-2' engraved along the capacitor pack. Serial number micro-etched on underside. No additional branding — corporate restraint.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained, slightly worn. Field-calibrated units show micro-scoring on the emitter shroud from adjustment sessions. Capacitor casing may have scuff marks from carrying harnesses. Typically pristine internally — these weapons require regular calibration and are rarely allowed to deteriorate.
